annotation.title_clean: Designing Social Robots with Ethical, User-Adaptive Explainability in the Era of Foundation Models
annotation.title_en: Designing Social Robots with Ethical, User-Adaptive Explainability in the Era of Foundation Models
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Doğan, F.I.; Markelius, A.; Gunes, H.
annotation.venue: HRI Companion '26 (ACM/IEEE International Conference on Human-Robot Interaction); arXiv
annotation.summary_en: Position paper arguing that ethical, user-adapted explainability should be a core design objective for foundation-model-driven social robots. It identifies open challenges, proposes four recommendations (user-adapted, modality-aware, co-designed explanations built on smaller, fairer datasets), and illustrates them with an LLM-driven socially assistive robot.
key_provisions_or_claims: One-size-fits-all explanations are inadequate for foundation-model-driven social robots.
Four recommendations: user-adapted, modality-aware, co-designed explanation strategies using smaller, curated, fairer datasets.
Layered adaptation: adapt to broad user clusters first, then refine with interaction data.
Explanations can create illusions of competence, over-trust and anthropomorphism, so they should signal uncertainty and limits.
Illustrative use case: LLM-driven socially assistive robot in a sensitive domain.
